name: Peace of Utrecht and Hanseatic Decline
summary: The Peace of Utrecht (1474) between the Hanseatic League and England settled a trade war during which England had suspended Hanse privileges. The League retained its Steelyard privileges in London, but the settlement revealed its weakness: it could no longer exclude English merchants from the Baltic. As national monarchies centralized commercial policy, the city-based Hanse model of cooperative merchant power became progressively obsolete.
outcomes: English merchants gain access to Baltic
Beginning of Hanseatic decline as nation-states assert trade control
Commercial balance shifting toward individual monarchies

_quarry.structural_significance: Marked the beginning of the Hanseatic League's long decline as nation-states developed coherent commercial policies that superseded merchant city alliances.

sources_used: Lloyd, England and the German Hanse
